reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes the laser synthesis method and states that the defective carbon support stabilizes the nanoalloys, but it provides no data or discussion on high-temperature annealing, thermal stability, or comparative behavior against conventionally prepared samples. The key premises about high-temperature stability, slowed diffusion, and superiority over controls are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Ultrafast laser synthesis kinetically traps an equiatomic, disordered structure
Defective carbon support stabilizes metal atoms and inhibits diffusion
Kinetic trapping plus support interactions slows diffusion and phase segregation at high temperature
Conventional slow synthesis leads to phase segregation under similar heating
Stability advantage holds for particles <5 nm up to ~0.5 Tm
